profile.name: Mesfin Abraham Ali
profile.headline: Evidence on education, work and inequality in Ethiopia
profile.bio: I am Mesfin Abraham Ali, a development economist and PhD candidate at Wageningen University and Research. I study how schooling expanded across Ethiopia and what it did for jobs and living standards. I also take on evaluations, market studies and data verification.

researchProfile.title: Research Highlights and Interests
researchProfile.summary: My dissertation follows the expansion of formal education in Ethiopia from the mid nineteenth century and links it to labour markets, intergenerational mobility and structural change. It sits within the NWO Vici project South South Divergence, under Prof. Ewout Frankema.

projects.title: Doctoral dissertation
projects.subtitle: Educational expansion, labour markets and structural change in Ethiopia
projects.description: How the uneven spread of schools shaped jobs, mobility and inequality across generations.
projects.longDescription: The dissertation uses colonial and imperial administrative records, mission archives, government reports, census records and household surveys to build long run datasets. It applies panel econometrics and quasi experimental designs, including difference in differences and regression discontinuity, to estimate effects of educational infrastructure on labour market outcomes across generations. The early and unequal placement of schools produced regional and intergenerational gaps in access to skilled work that have proven persistent.
highlights: Archival records rebuilt into structured long run datasets
Quasi experimental estimates of the effect of school placement
Three chapters, each planned as a journal article

projects.title: EthioSkills
projects.subtitle: Advertised demand for skills in Ethiopia
projects.description: A daily record of Ethiopian job postings, turned into weekly and monthly reports.
projects.longDescription: EthioSkills collects job postings from more than ten Ethiopian job sites every day, standardises titles, places, education and experience requirements, and classifies each posting. It measures advertised demand only. It does not measure total employment, and informal work is largely invisible in this source. Reports state these limits next to each result.
highlights: More than ten job sites collected daily

projects.title: EthioGTS
projects.subtitle: A register of graduate tracer studies in Ethiopia
projects.description: Tracer studies made findable, checked against their sources and graded for quality.
projects.longDescription: The register holds 33 studies from 18 institutions. 11 are checked against the source document. 14 report an employment rate, ranging from 51.6 to 98.24 percent under 11 different wordings, so the rates are not comparable and the register never pools them. Response rates, employer data and results by gender are thinly reported. The project offers an annual report, a short decision brief and a minimum reporting standard for future studies.
highlights: Minimum reporting standard for future tracer studies

projects.title: Impact evaluation, BENEFIT REALISE
projects.subtitle: Wheat productivity and livelihoods in Arsi zone
projects.description: A quasi experimental evaluation of improved seed and capacity building for smallholders.
projects.longDescription: I was a member of the research team that evaluated whether capacity building and improved seed raised smallholder productivity under the Dutch funded BENEFIT REALISE programme. The team combined focus group discussions and key informant interviews with a household survey of 202 farm households, compared with a baseline of 200 households. I took part in supervising data collection and in data entry and management in SPSS and Stata. Wheat yield in the main intervention area rose by 593 kilograms per hectare relative to the comparison area, significant at the 5 percent level.
highlights: Mixed methods with a household survey
Wheat yield gain of 593 kilograms per hectare
Recommendations on evaluation timing and data reliability

projects.title: Midterm evaluation, Tulu Moye
projects.subtitle: SOS Children's Villages Ethiopia
projects.description: A midterm evaluation of child development interventions.
projects.longDescription: I contributed to a midterm evaluation of the Tulu Moye Child Development Project. The work tracked case records through defined program stages, examined why some cases did not progress as expected, assessed performance against the project objectives, and produced an evaluation report with recommendations for program management.
highlights: Case records tracked through program stages

projects.title: Investment feasibility study
projects.subtitle: Oromia Public Enterprises Supervisory Agency
projects.description: A two stage assessment of proposed tourism and investment projects.
projects.longDescription: I contributed to a feasibility study of proposed tourism and investment projects across several development sites. Projects were scored on qualitative indicators and classified as potential or not. Potential projects went through an economic evaluation using the internal rate of return, and the highest scoring project was recommended to the regional government. I organised the indicator data and compiled the investment and revenue figures for the final comparison.

highlights: Internal rate of return for potential projects
